name: Zalm
english_description: Zalm sits at the Scorched Gates, where the Damar River descends from the Nahasa Desert and starts its journey through the Jarjara Escarpment. The silt brought by the river produces bountiful crops of wheat.

name: Mabwaz
english_description: Mabwaz overlooks the Damar River as it weaves through the mesas of the Jarjara Escarpment. Villagers grow wheat and other crops in the silt of the river floodplain.

name: Nahlan
english_description: Nahlan sits on the floodplain of the Damar River as it cuts through the Jarjara Escarpment. This soil, refreshed yearly by the silt of the flooding river, produces bountiful crops of wheat.

name: Hamoshawat
english_description: Hamoshawat lies on the lower Damar river, just before it reaches the Bahr al-Yeshm sea. The rich silt deposits left by the river make this one of the most fertile regions of the Aserai lands.

name: Mijayit
english_description: Mijayit lies off of the estuary of the Damar river as it reaches the Bahr al-Yeshm sea. The rich silt deposits left by the river make this one of the most fertile regions and densely populated regions of the Aserai lands.

name: Qidnar
english_description: Qidnar sits on the landward side of the Jarjara Escarpment, looking down onto the deep desert of the central Nahasa. Here, the fierce rains that come once every few years fall onto rocky hills replete with clefts and crevaces, and can be diverted with channels into peaceful palm-gardens.

name: Bait Hatif
english_description: Bait Hatif lies in one of the wadis that are cut through the Jarjara Escarpment by the rare but fierce desert rains. Wells tap the groundwater here and allow subsistence farming, but the wealth of the land comes from the fine horses raised on the grasses that grow on the heights in the spring.

name: Abba
english_description: Abba sits in a broad wadi of the Jarjara Escarpment, close to the outlet where the rains that fall once every few years rush down to the sea. Runoff from the hills is trapped underground here, sustaining an oasis. Wheat thrives in the fields and gardens.

name: Asmait
english_description: Asmait lies in a nook of the red sandstone Jabal Ashabi mountains, bordered to the south by the deep desert. Villagers trap floods running down the hills during rare rainstorms, using the water to grow date palms and other crops.
